new_bugs.title: A provider message moved between queues can wait for ever, and then every timer run stops on it
new_bugs.where: /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/src/server/routes-billing.ts applyStripeEvent lines 1647 to 1658 (inQueue re-keys from inside a running queue item) and billingRetries inbox loop lines 1395 to 1408
new_bugs.detail: Probes /home/user/treegens-app/sign-and-grow/tests/out/verify-pay-core/b-today.ts Q1 and q1-tick.ts. Steps: a message for provider customer cus_loop waits in queue provider:cus_loop; the account gets that customer id, so at its turn the message moves into the account's queue (behind a renewal); before it runs there, the account's customer id changes back, so it moves to provider:cus_loop again, whose tail is its own first half. Result: 'the refund notice: still waiting after 8 s'; a Cancel press for that account 'still waiting after 3 s'. Delivered through the webhook it is answered 'received' and stays in the inbox; then tick() never returns ('the timer run is still waiting after 6 s', twice), so everything after billingRetries in cron.ts (dormancy nudges, switched-off codes, purgeClosedAccounts, supportTick) stops for every account until a restart. The precondition (an account's stripe_customer_id changing twice within seconds, e.g. adopt() overwriting it and withCustomer/portal clearing it on 'No such customer') is rare. Fix: re-key at most once (pass a flag; if the key changes again, run in place), or compute the key without re-queueing from inside serial(); give each inbox row a time limit in the timer (Promise.race with a timeout) so one stuck message cannot hold the tick.
